Still there. The fear of being watched? Worse. No mood episode, just the voices in my head and the crawling. I don’t need sleep, my mind races, and everything feels alive—the shadows on the wall, the patterns in the wallpaper, even the clock ticking pulls my attention like it’s shouting at me. I’ll start talking and the words just spill out, sometimes jumping around so much even I can’t follow them. My daughter says she can’t understand me anymore.

There are times I see people standing in the corners of rooms—my late wife, once, or strangers watching me. I know, rationally, they’re not real, but they look so solid. I’ve started thinking the neighbors are spying through the vents, planting things in my mail. I don’t trust the TV either—the newscasters blink too much, like they’re sending me coded messages.

Before all this, I just stopped caring. I didn’t want to fish, didn’t want to see anyone. I even laid out my pills once, thought about ending it. But that passed—now I’m back to feeling electric, like I could fix the whole house in one night. Truth is, I can’t tell when one state ends and the other begins. The voices and visions don’t always go away when the high does. Or maybe they do—I’m not sure anymore.

I felt electric, on top of the world, even when neighbors said I was acting strange. But along with that, I began seeing things—my late wife standing in the hallway, people outside the window watching me. I know it sounds wild, but they felt real. I became convinced someone was spying on me, maybe the government, tracking my thoughts. My speech must’ve gotten messy—my daughter said I wasn’t making sense, jumping from topic to topic like signals in the static of an old radio.  

Then, about three months ago, it all crashed. I stopped caring, couldn’t get off the couch. The things I used to love, like gardening, didn’t matter. I even took a bunch of pills one night—not because I wanted to go, but because I didn’t know how to stop the voices and images, how to make my head quiet. What’s worse is that even now, when I’m not manic or depressed—just calm—the shadows and voices still come. I’ve been like this for over a year—almost two now—and it’s wrecking everything. I can’t sleep, not that I want to. Resting feels pointless. I’m always moving, fixing things, starting projects—rewired the whole house, redid the gutters, bought a generator… never finish one thing, but I don’t care. Small stuff sets me off, though. My wife asked me to hang a picture last week, and I yelled at her like she’d betrayed me. I know it’s too much, but the anger just erupts.

There’s this smell—like burning plastic or dead wires—it follows me everywhere. I used to think it was the panels overheating on the roof, but I’ve checked them. Nothing’s burning. It’s in my truck, in the house, even outside. And I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced something big’s coming. The grid’s going to fail. The sun’s going to wipe everything clean. Not in years—*soon*. Like, any day now. The world’s rotting from the inside.

She says I’m not making sense. I told her the air itself is toxic, that the government’s hiding the data. I keep working because if I stop, I think I’ll vanish. But I don’t know… do I only think this when I’m wired like this? Or does it stay, even when I’m not? I can’t tell the difference anymore.
D006-D010_h006.question_a:

I started getting this buzzing energy—couldn’t sit still, barely slept, didn’t even need it. I’d start wiring one array, then jump to testing inverters, then drive to another job site for no reason. My wife says I was snapping at her over nothing, like she’d move a tool and I’d yell.

And the smells—burnt plastic, sewage, something rotting—even when no one else smells anything. I know how it sounds, but I *know* what I’m smelling. I started believing the grid was going to fail globally—solar systems would stop working, society would collapse. I still believe it, honestly.

But here's the thing—the worst part isn’t just the mania. Even when I’m not wired, not irritable, when I’m actually resting… the smells come back. The thoughts come back. That fear doesn’t go away. It’s been like this for weeks at a time, even when I’m not manic. It’s not just the mood driving it—this stuff sticks around on its own.

But here’s the thing—the voices, the smells, the certainty that it’s all over—they only hit when I’m in this wired-up state. When the high fades, it all goes quiet. I don’t hear it. I don’t smell it. I’m just… exhausted. So if it’s only during these manic spikes, then it’s not like I’m losing touch all the time, right? Just during the storm.

D006-D010_h025.question_both:
I’ve been struggling for over a year, maybe closer to two, I can’t keep track anymore. Work’s been up and down—there was a stretch where I was running on nothing, barely sleeping, just going, going, going. Felt like I could weld 24/7, started two side jobs, called up old friends outta the blue, even drove up to my brother’s place one night on a whim. Didn’t feel tired. Felt unstoppable. But then it flipped—started crying for no reason, couldn’t get out of bed, food tasted like ash. That low patch lasted months.

And all through it, there's this… stuff. I know it sounds off, but I can *feel* things under my skin—like bugs crawling, or wires tightening around my legs. Doctors find nothing, but I *know* something’s wrong inside. My body’s shutting down. Sometimes when I talk, the words just… slide into rhymes, like my mouth’s playing tricks. My wife says I’m not making sense. I’ve stopped calling people. Even my buddies from the shop—I just don’t want to hear their voices.

The highs, the lows, the sensations—it all blurs. Some days I’m wired, others I’m frozen. I can’t say exactly when one starts and the other stops.
D006-D010_h025.question_a:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now. At first, it was like I caught lightning—I was welding double shifts, barely sleeping, full of energy, calling old friends, making big plans. I felt like I didn’t need rest, like my body was running on something stronger than blood. But even when that high faded, the voices didn’t come—wait, no—my skin *crawls*, like something’s burrowing under it, especially my arms where I weld. Doctors find nothing, but I *know* there’s metal shavings stuck in my nerves. That’s real to me.  

For nine months, I’ve felt this itch, this pull under my skin, and I’m convinced my liver’s melting—I can *feel* it rotting. My wife says I talk funny—stuff like “sparks start the dark, so hark the lark”—but it makes sense to me. I just don’t see people anymore. Don’t want to.  

The wild energy lasted a full year—spent our savings on a welding rig I never built, drove like a maniac. Then I crashed: couldn’t get out of bed, food tasted dead, cried over nothing. But here’s the thing—*even when the highs and lows passed*, the crawling, the delusions, the word-jumbles—they stayed. For weeks after I wasn’t manic or depressed, I still felt the bugs under my skin, still believed my body was breaking down. That’s not just mood—that’s something else. Something stuck.
D006-D010_h025.question_b:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—work’s hard, my wife’s worried, and I just can’t keep things together. About a year ago, I suddenly felt on top of the world. I was full of energy, barely sleeping—like four hours and I was wide awake, itching to go. I’d weld extra jobs, start renovations at home, call people in the middle of the night to hang out. I wasn’t reckless? Nah—I drove like a maniac once or twice, took some pills at a party, things I’d never do sober. I felt bulletproof.

But during that time, things got… weird. I became convinced my organs were rotting—doctors say I’m fine, but I *felt* it. Like bugs crawling under my skin, even now sometimes. I’d say things like “I’m a spark in the dark, lighting the lark,” just because it sounded sharp—my wife said I wasn’t making sense. I stopped calling friends, didn’t want the noise—they couldn’t understand.

When that high crashed, I flattened out. Started crying over nothing. Couldn’t eat. Took forever to fall asleep. Even lifting a wrench felt heavy. That lasted months. But the key thing? The bugs, the rhyming, the body beliefs—they *only* came during that crazy high spell. Never before, never since.
